messages:
Ashley L.: Quick design review: latency panel responsiveness + sampling controls. Dropped a mock and notes in the doc. TL;DR — keep p95 visible at narrow widths, de-emphasize sampling (move out of primary header), tighten timepicker microcopy and a11y fixes.

Mike R.: Saw the mock — nice. One worry: at 320px the p95 sparkline vanishes. Right now we hide percentiles at narrow widths. Can we stack percentile pills below the chart instead of hiding them? :thinking_face:

Ashley L.: Yes — stacking is my preference. Proposed: chart stays full width, then a compact row of percentile pills (p50 / p95 / p99) beneath. Each pill expands on hover to show exact value and small tooltip. Keeps main metric visible on mobile.

Jon P.: Strong +1. Also the timepicker CTA is confusing — users expect something like 'Update range' or 'Apply range' not just 'Apply'. My vote: 'Update range'.

Priya S.: I prefer 'Apply range' — concise and clear. 'Update range' reads slightly heavier to me.

Ashley L.: Candidate microcopy list for quick A/B: 'Apply', 'Apply range', 'Update range', 'Show results', 'Refresh range'. We should pick two for a small test.

Olivia N.: A11y nits: the timepicker modal doesn't trap focus — keyboard users can tab out to background controls. Also when streaming data updates the p95 number, we should have aria-live='polite' on that element so screen readers announce changes without being spammy.

Sam K.: Performance note: current heatmap implementation renders ~12k DOM rects for a 24h view with fine buckets — this causes jank on low-end devices. Options: server-side downsampling when viewport small, or switch heatmap to canvas rendering for many buckets.

Mike R.: Canvas for the dense heatmap + SVG for percentiles seems reasonable. That keeps interactivity for the pills but gives speed for the expensive part. Aligns with our charting lib's hybrid approach.

Ashley L.: Sampling control placement: right now it's a primary control in the header and users toggle it by accident. Suggest moving it into the overflow menu as 'Sampling settings' with an inline quick toggle 'Auto-sampling' visible in the collapsed menu.

Jon P.: On Auto-sampling rules: idea — if queries/sec > X or estimated tiles > Y then coarsen sampling automatically, else show full detail. Also add a small, non-blocking toast: 'Sampling increased to 1:10 for performance' with an undo button.

Priya S.: Microcopy for the toggle: 'Auto-sampling (recommended)' vs 'Sampling: auto/manual'. I think the first reads friendlier.

Olivia N.: For keyboard and screen reader labels: use aria-label='Toggle auto sampling' and ensure the toast uses role='status' so it's announced. Also respect prefers-reduced-motion for any heatmap animation.

Ashley L.: Small CSS snippet for reduced motion so we capture that behavior (will include in spec):

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .heatmap {
    transition: none !important;
    animation: none !important;
  }
}
```

Sam K.: I'll prototype server-side downsampling this week. Question: what metric should be the primary trigger for auto-sampling? Jon suggested queries/sec, but render cost estimate might be better (tiles-to-render).

Jon P.: Let's use a combined heuristic: tiles-to-render estimate + queries/sec. I'll draft thresholds (e.g., tiles > 2000 OR qps > 50 -> enable coarse sampling) and post by Friday.

Ashley L.: Action items: Mike — update responsive mock with stacked percentile pills and canvas heatmap note; Olivia — short a11y checklist for timepicker + aria-live; Sam — prototype server-side downsampling; Jon — threshold proposal; Priya — 3 microcopy variants with short rationale. Sync Friday 11am in #design. Thanks everyone! :pray:
